name: WellSaid Labs
subcategory: synthetic voice, dubbing and AI avatars
tagline: Produce clearly labeled voiceovers from user-authored scripts using licensed local voices

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 3 downloaded minutes/month; 10 generated minutes; 3 active projects; 1 seat
tiers.notes: No commercial usage rights; 24 kHz MP3 export.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 20 downloaded minutes/month monthly, or 240 downloaded minutes/year annual; 10 projects; 1 seat
tiers.notes: Annual plan is $120/year; extra download minutes can be purchased in Studio.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 180 downloaded minutes/month monthly, or 2,160 downloaded minutes/year annual; unlimited projects; 1 seat
tiers.notes: Annual plan is $396/year; extra download minutes can be purchased in Studio.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.notes: Annual-only at $1,920/year/user; onboarding/training and dedicated customer success are offered only above 3 licenses.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom downloaded minutes/year/user and custom seat count

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 downloaded minutes/month, 10 generated minutes, 3 active projects, 1 seat, and no commercial rights
pricing.billingTerms: individual plans monthly + annual; Business and Enterprise annual only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid plans include finite downloaded-audio minutes even though generation is unlimited; extra download minutes cost extra, and Business support/onboarding benefits are gated above 3 licenses.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For WellSaid Labs, produce clearly labeled voiceovers from user-authored scripts using licensed local voices. The hard boundary is premium proprietary voices, enterprise rights, pronunciation tools, workflow, and support, plus models, compute, rights, and safety operations.
coreLoopDIY: Produce clearly labeled synthetic voiceovers from user-authored scripts using licensed local voices, and retain provenance for every output.
requirements: voices the user has rights and consent to use
whatYouLose: premium proprietary voices, enterprise rights, pronunciation tools, workflow, and support
moderation, consent verification, and enterprise rights
moatNotes: models, compute, rights, and safety operations
ongoingBurden: model licensing, consent records, impersonation risk, watermarking, GPU queues, media storage, abuse response, and rapid model changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for WellSaid Labs because customers pay for output quality, production speed, licensed voices, consent workflows, and a provider that carries the operational risk. The recurring cost buys model licensing, consent records, impersonation risk, watermarking, GPU queues, media storage, abuse response, and rapid model changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Piper
priorArt.desc: Active community continuation of the fast local Piper text-to-speech engine.

alternatives.name: Balabolka
alternatives.desc: Plain licensed system voices from script to audio, with none of the brand theatre.

facts.install: Run the Windows installer or unzip the portable build
facts.engines: Microsoft Speech API 4/5 and Microsoft Speech Platform voices installed on Windows; an optional separate utility can call online TTS services
facts.dataFormat: Input documents and generated WAV, MP3, MP4, OGG or WMA audio plus optional LRC/SRT files on local disk
facts.gapVsPaid: Balabolka's free terms are personal and non-commercial, and Windows system voices do not provide WellSaid's curated commercial voice rights or team review.
facts.setupBlocker: Balabolka includes no voices, so the desired Windows SAPI voice or language pack must already be installed

alternatives.name: TTS WebUI
alternatives.desc: A local Windows voice workbench with many engines and saved outputs; consistency varies with the model.

facts.install: On Windows install TTS WebUI Ignition with winget; otherwise use a release/legacy installer or Docker
facts.engines: Extension-driven local models including Bark, Tortoise, MMS, Vall-E X, StyleTTS2, SeamlessM4T, XTTSv2, F5-TTS, Parler-TTS, OpenVoice, Kokoro, DIA, CosyVoice, GPT-SoVITS, Piper and Chatterbox
facts.dataFormat: Downloaded model caches, generated audio files and metadata in local installation/data directories; SQLite can hold generated-audio metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: Voice consistency and commercial-use rights vary by model, with none of WellSaid's managed approval, pronunciation and collaboration workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The base install is about 10.7 GB, models add several gigabytes each, and GPU/CUDA or extension dependency conflicts are common

alternatives.name: Voicebox
alternatives.desc: Reusable local voice profiles, long-form scripts and exportable audio without a character meter.

facts.install: Install the macOS DMG or Windows MSI; Docker is supported, while Linux currently requires a source installation
facts.engines: Qwen3-TTS, Qwen CustomVoice, LuxTTS, Chatterbox Multilingual, Chatterbox Turbo, HumeAI TADA and Kokoro; Whisper/Whisper Turbo for speech-to-text; local Qwen3 models for refinement and personas
facts.dataFormat: SQLite plus model, voice-profile, generated-audio and capture files in the local Voicebox data directory; original audio and transcripts stay on device
facts.gapVsPaid: Local cloned and open models do not provide WellSaid's vetted commercial voice catalog, team collaboration or consistent studio QA.
facts.setupBlocker: Large model downloads and choosing a hardware backend; Linux has no prebuilt binary yet

rejectedAlternatives.name: AllTalk TTS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Often suggested for local voiceovers, but the supported path still looks like a development environment.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Creative plan and a clearly labeled local synthetic-media tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for WellSaid Labs in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ffmpeg, and a user-owned local TTS model; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: produce clearly labeled synthetic voiceovers from user-authored scripts using licensed local voices, and retain provenance for every output.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Require a project-level rights and consent acknowledgement before generating audio.
Ship with no celebrity, public-figure, or scraped voice assets and accept only explicitly licensed models.
Generate speech from text with voice, speed, pause, pronunciation, and segment controls.
Create a timeline for audio, captions, uploaded visuals, and simple transitions.
Embed project metadata and a visible synthetic-media disclosure in exported assets.
Store prompts, model identifiers, consent notes, and output hashes in a local provenance log.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out cloning a voice without clear consent.
Deliberately leave out impersonation or deceptive unlabeled media.
Deliberately leave out a frontier avatar model, public hosting, or enterprise rights clearance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
